meaning.en: So close that not even a hair could pass between; an extremely critical, urgent moment.
meaning.zh: 中间容不下一根头发，形容情势极其危急或相距极近。

examples.zh: 消防员在间不容发之际把孩子救了出来。
examples.en: The firefighter pulled the child out at the very last moment.

examples.zh: 比赛进入间不容发的最后一分钟。
examples.en: The match entered a nail-biting final minute.

story.en: Mei Cheng warned the King of Wu that disaster comes from small beginnings and, when it arrives, there is 'no room for a hair' between survival and ruin.
story.zh: 枚乘劝吴王：“其出不出，间不容发。”

usage.en: Describes a critical moment; 间 is read jiàn (gap), not jiān. Often with 之际/时刻.
usage.zh: 形容情势危急；“间”读 jiàn，常与“之际、时刻”搭配。

meaning.en: Winding like the bowels; describes deep sorrow that tangles the heart or a long, twisting route.
meaning.zh: 形容心中忧思痛苦，百转千回；也形容道路、河流等曲折。

examples.zh: 这首曲子婉转低回，听得人九曲回肠。
examples.en: The melody is mournful and winding, and it wrenches the heart.

examples.zh: 想起离乡的日子，他不禁九曲回肠。
examples.en: Remembering the days of leaving home, he was wrung with sorrow.

story.en: Sima Qian wrote that in his grief 'the bowels turn nine times a day' (肠一日而九回).
story.zh: “是以肠一日而九回，居则忽忽若有所亡。”

usage.en: Literary; mostly of sorrow or heavy feelings, sometimes of winding rivers. Often 柔肠/愁肠 style.
usage.zh: 书面语，多形容愁思，也可形容曲折的河道。

natural: strung with evils to the brim

meaning.en: So many evil deeds that the measure is full and punishment is due.
meaning.zh: 罪恶累积到了极点，已到受惩罚的时候。

equivalents: his crimes have caught up with him

examples.zh: 这个恶贯满盈的罪犯终于落网了。
examples.en: The thoroughly wicked criminal was finally caught.

examples.zh: 恶贯满盈者，终将受到法律的制裁。
examples.en: Those whose crimes are piled high will in the end be punished by law.

story.en: The Book of Documents says of the tyrant Shang (Zhou): his crimes strung together are full (商罪贯盈), and Heaven bids us punish him.
story.zh: 《尚书·泰誓上》：“商罪贯盈，天命诛之。”

date.zh: 东晋 · 约4世纪初（伪古文《尚书》篇章）
date.en: Eastern Jin, early 4th c. (spurious “Old Text” chapter of the Book of Documents)

usage.en: Strongly derogatory; modifies a person who has done much evil. 恶 is è here.
usage.zh: 贬义很重，修饰作恶多端的人；“恶”读 è。

meaning.en: To ask a question when you already know the answer, whether to tease or to provoke.
meaning.zh: 明明知道，却故意去问。

equivalents: ask a question one knows the answer to

examples.zh: 你明知故问，他当然不想去。
examples.en: You know perfectly well; of course he doesn't want to go.

examples.zh: 她明知故问地笑着说：“谁送你的花呀？”
examples.en: She asked with a knowing smile, 'Who sent you the flowers?'

usage.en: Can be playful or mildly accusing; used as predicate or adverbial.
usage.zh: 可带调侃或责备，作谓语、状语。

meaning.en: To be willing to do something, however hard or risky; not to refuse in any case.
meaning.zh: 无论怎样艰难危险，都不推辞，表示愿意去做。

equivalents: will gladly do whatever it takes

examples.zh: 只要国家需要，我们赴汤蹈火也在所不辞。
examples.en: If the country needs us, we won't shirk even fire and water.

examples.zh: 为了朋友，即便得罪人也在所不辞。
examples.en: For my friends I would do it even at the cost of offending others.

usage.en: Positive; usually follows a condition and 也: …也在所不辞.
usage.zh: 褒义，常用于“……也在所不辞”。

natural: the dragon's pool and tiger's den

meaning.en: A place of great danger, like a dragon's pool or a tiger's den.
meaning.zh: 比喻极其危险的地方。

examples.zh: 为了救人，他单枪匹马闯入龙潭虎穴。
examples.en: To rescue someone he went alone into the lion's den.

examples.zh: 别看这里平静，说不定就是龙潭虎穴。
examples.en: It looks calm, but it may be a very dangerous place.

usage.en: Neutral in tone; often with 闯/入/深入. Also describes a daunting place, not only a physical one.
usage.zh: 中性，常与“闯、入、深入”搭配。

meaning.en: Experienced and steady in conduct: cautious, mature and reliable.
meaning.zh: 办事老练稳重，不轻举妄动。

examples.zh: 他虽然年轻，却老成持重，大家都愿意把事交给他。
examples.en: Though young, he is mature and steady, and everyone trusts him with work.

examples.zh: 这位老成持重的经理从不轻易表态。
examples.en: The level-headed manager never commits himself lightly.

usage.en: Praise; can describe a young person who acts older than their years. Sometimes slightly implies over-caution.
usage.zh: 褒义，可形容年轻人像老人一样稳重。

meaning.en: To feel extremely fortunate, as if blessed over three lifetimes; a polite remark when meeting someone.
meaning.zh: 三世都有福气，形容非常幸运，多用作客套话。

examples.zh: 今日得见先生，真是三生有幸。
examples.en: Meeting you today, sir, is a great honour.

examples.zh: 能与您合作，我们三生有幸。
examples.en: We are blessed to work with you.

usage.en: A courteous phrase for first meetings; polite or slightly flowery. 三生: past, present and future lives (Buddhist).
usage.zh: 多作客套话；“三生”指前生、今生、来生。

meaning.en: To fail to appreciate being treated kindly or favourably; ungrateful.
meaning.zh: 不懂得别人对自己的器重和好意。

equivalents: not know when one is well off

examples.zh: 经理给你升职的机会，你还推三阻四，真是不识抬举。
examples.en: The manager offers you a promotion and you keep dithering; you don't know your luck.

examples.zh: 别不识抬举，我是好心帮你。
examples.en: Don't be ungrateful; I'm trying to help you.

usage.en: Used by the person offering the favour; slightly scolding. Often in warnings: 别不识抬举.
usage.zh: 多出自施惠者之口，带责备，常说“别不识抬举”。

synonyms: 敬酒不吃吃罚酒——不知好歹

meaning.en: Numerous and of all kinds.
meaning.zh: 形容众多、种类繁多。

examples.zh: 商场里林林总总的商品让人眼花缭乱。
examples.en: The great variety of goods in the mall dazzles the eye.

examples.zh: 他列出了林林总总的理由。
examples.en: He listed all sorts of reasons.

usage.en: Neutral; attributive before a noun (林林总总的…). Do not use of a single large item.
usage.zh: 中性，多作定语：“林林总总的……”。

meaning.en: Extremely timid, scared of everything.
meaning.zh: 胆子小得像老鼠一样，形容非常胆怯。

examples.zh: 他胆小如鼠，一听到打雷就躲进被窝。
examples.en: He is as timid as a mouse and hides under the covers at thunder.

examples.zh: 别看他个子高，其实胆小如鼠。
examples.en: He may be tall, but he is a coward at heart.

usage.en: Mildly mocking; used of people. Opposite of 胆大包天.
usage.zh: 略带嘲讽，用于人。

antonyms: 吃了熊心豹子胆——胆大包天
老虎头上拍苍蝇——胆子不小
旗杆上扎鸡毛——好大的胆（掸）子
撑死胆大的，饿死胆小的

meaning.en: To murder people and rob them of their goods: banditry.
meaning.zh: 杀害人命，抢夺财物，指强盗行为。

examples.zh: 这伙匪徒杀人越货，无恶不作。
examples.en: The gang of bandits murder and rob and stop at nothing.

examples.zh: 警方破获了一起杀人越货的重大案件。
examples.en: Police solved a serious case of robbery and murder.

story.en: The Book of Documents, speaking of crimes punishable by death, includes those who 'kill people and seize goods' (杀越人于货).
story.zh: 《康诰》：“杀越人于货，暋不畏死，罔弗憝。”

date.zh: 西周至战国 · 前11—前3世纪
date.en: Western Zhou to Warring States, 11th–3rd c. BC

usage.en: Strongly derogatory; legal/news register. 越 = seize.
usage.zh: 贬义极强，多见于法制、新闻语体；“越”意为抢夺。

meaning.en: Bright eyes and pearly teeth; a description of a beautiful woman.
meaning.zh: 明亮的眼睛，洁白的牙齿，形容女子容貌美丽。

examples.zh: 她明眸皓齿，笑起来格外动人。
examples.en: With bright eyes and pearly teeth, she is especially lovely when she smiles.

examples.zh: 画中人明眸皓齿，神态温婉。
examples.en: The woman in the painting has bright eyes, white teeth and a gentle air.

story.en: Du Fu lamented the dead Consort Yang: 'Where are her bright eyes and white teeth now?'
story.zh: 杜甫《哀江头》：“明眸皓齿今何在？血污游魂归不得。”

usage.en: Literary, of women's beauty; describes the person, not a general scene.
usage.zh: 书面语，形容女子美貌。

meaning.en: To slander someone with vicious accusations.
meaning.zh: 用恶毒的话诬蔑、辱骂别人。

examples.zh: 你拿不出证据就别血口喷人！
examples.en: Don't slander people if you can't produce proof!

examples.zh: 他被血口喷人，气得直发抖。
examples.en: Maliciously slandered, he shook with anger.

usage.en: Strong accusation, often 你别血口喷人. Often used with 含血喷人 as a close form.
usage.zh: 指责对方诬陷时用，语气强烈；常说“你别血口喷人”。

meaning.en: Pretended kindness and righteousness: hypocrisy that conceals selfish motives.
meaning.zh: 表面上装作仁慈、有道义，实际上虚伪。

examples.zh: 他那副假仁假义的嘴脸让人作呕。
examples.en: His hypocritical, sanctimonious face is sickening.

examples.zh: 别被他假仁假义的样子骗了。
examples.en: Don't be fooled by his show of virtue.

usage.en: Derogatory; describes people who pose as kind or moral. Not the same as 虚情假意, which is about emotions.
usage.zh: 贬义，指装作仁义的人。

meaning.en: To keep one's integrity as spotless as jade: originally sexual chastity, now also moral purity.
meaning.zh: 像爱惜玉一样保持自身的纯洁，多指不失贞操，也比喻洁身自好。

examples.zh: 他在名利场中守身如玉，从不同流合污。
examples.en: In a world of fame and profit he kept himself spotless and never went along with the crowd.

examples.zh: 她对婚姻忠贞，守身如玉。
examples.en: She was faithful in marriage and kept herself pure.

usage.en: Positive; modern usage also covers moral and professional integrity. Older sense about chastity can sound dated.
usage.zh: 褒义；现也指品行端正，旧义指贞洁，略显陈旧。

meaning.en: To stay orderly and unruffled even when busy or under pressure; calm and composed.
meaning.zh: 在紧张忙碌中仍保持从容不迫、有条不紊。

examples.zh: 大战在即，他却好整以暇地泡了一壶茶。
examples.en: With a big battle at hand, he calmly brewed a pot of tea.

examples.zh: 面对记者的提问，她好整以暇，对答如流。
examples.en: Facing the reporters, she stayed composed and answered fluently.

story.en: The Zuo Zhuan says of the Jin army that they 'like to be orderly in their ranks and like to take their time' (好以众整，好以暇).

usage.en: Praise for composure. 好 is read hào (to like), and 暇 xiá; commonly misused to mean 'having lots of free time'.
usage.zh: 褒义；“好”读 hào，常被误解为“空闲无事”。

meaning.en: Petty, misplaced kindness that lacks the resolve needed for great matters.
meaning.zh: 指处事优柔寡断、不分轻重的小仁小惠。

examples.zh: 商场如战场，不能讲妇人之仁。
examples.en: Business is a battlefield, and there's no room for soft-heartedness.

examples.zh: 他对下属一味妇人之仁，导致纪律松懈。
examples.en: He was too soft with his staff, and discipline slackened.

story.en: Han Xin said of Xiang Yu: he is kind and gentle but cannot bring himself to reward his men with titles; this is 'a woman's kindness'.
story.zh: 韩信评项羽：“此所谓妇人之仁也。”

usage.en: Mildly derogatory; the wording can sound sexist today, so use it for the idea of misplaced leniency, not about women.
usage.zh: 略含贬义，现代使用时需留意有性别偏见之嫌。

meaning.en: A trivial skill or minor accomplishment; often said modestly of one's own work.
meaning.zh: 微不足道的技能，常用作自谦或贬低他人的小本领。

equivalents: a mere trifle of a skill

examples.zh: 这点儿雕虫小技，不值得一提。
examples.en: This little trick is hardly worth mentioning.

examples.zh: 他靠一些雕虫小技糊弄了上司。
examples.en: He fooled his boss with a few cheap tricks.

story.en: Yang Xiong said that carving insect-script and seal characters was a trifle which a real man would not take up.
story.zh: 扬雄：“童子雕虫篆刻。……壮夫不为也。”

date.zh: 西汉末至新 · 前1世纪—1世纪
date.en: late Western Han to Xin, 1st c. BC–1st c. AD

usage.en: Can be modest about oneself (polite) or disdainful about others; note which from context. Often 雕虫小技，不足挂齿.
usage.zh: 自谦或轻视他人均可，视语境而定。

meaning.en: Vicious ambition that is in one's nature, like a wolf cub that cannot be tamed.
meaning.zh: 狼崽子生性凶残，比喻坏人本性难改、野心勃勃。

examples.zh: 他狼子野心，早就想取代董事长。
examples.en: He has a predatory ambition and long wanted to replace the chairman.

examples.zh: 别对狼子野心的人抱有幻想。
examples.en: Don't harbour illusions about people with such a ruthless ambition.

story.en: A Chu minister, hearing the infant Yuejiao cry like a wolf, urged that he be killed, for a wolf cub has a wild heart that cannot be tamed.
story.zh: 楚国大臣听出越椒哭声如狼，认为应除掉他：“狼子野心，是乃狼也，其可畜乎？”

usage.en: Strongly derogatory; used of power-hungry people, rulers, or states.
usage.zh: 贬义，多指野心勃勃的人或国家。

natural: how high the heavens, how thick the earth

meaning.en: The height of the sky and the depth of the earth; usually in 不知天高地厚, meaning one has no sense of one's limits.
meaning.zh: 天有多高、地有多厚；常说“不知天高地厚”，指不知道事情的深浅。

equivalents: not know how high the heavens are

examples.zh: 这个刚毕业的小伙子，真是不知天高地厚。
examples.en: This young graduate really doesn't know his limits.

examples.zh: 她深知天高地厚，做事从来谨慎。
examples.en: She has a good sense of proportion and is always careful.

usage.en: Almost always in the negative: 不知天高地厚, mildly scolding. Also expresses a vast, immense favour (e.g. 天高地厚之恩).
usage.zh: 几乎总是“不知天高地厚”，略带责备；也可指恩情深厚。

meaning.en: Formulaic official writing, full of empty phrases and no substance.
meaning.zh: 指内容空洞、徒具形式的官场文章或套话。

examples.zh: 这份报告全是官样文章，没有一点实质内容。
examples.en: The report is all bureaucratic boilerplate and has no real content.

examples.zh: 会议上讲了一堆官样文章，大家都听腻了。
examples.en: The meeting was full of stock phrases and everyone was tired of it.

usage.en: Derogatory; describes reports, speeches and documents. Not the same as 官腔 (tone of speech).
usage.zh: 贬义，指文件、讲话等；与“官腔”（语气）不同。

meaning.en: Head bowed and ears flat, like a docile dog: meekly obedient and servile.
meaning.zh: 低着头，耳朵贴下，像驯服的狗一样，形容十分顺从听话。

examples.zh: 他在老板面前总是俯首帖耳，从不敢说半个不字。
examples.en: In front of his boss he is always meekly submissive and never says no.

examples.zh: 对方态度强硬，他只得俯首帖耳地答应了。
examples.en: The other side was firm, so he meekly gave in.

story.en: Han Yu wrote that a creature that 'lowers its head, flattens its ears, wags its tail and begs for pity' is not what a hero would be.
story.zh: 韩愈：“若俯首帖耳，摇尾而乞怜者，非我之志也。”

usage.en: Derogatory; implies servility. 帖 is tiē here (not tiě/tiè).
usage.zh: 贬义，含奴颜婢膝之意；“帖”读 tiē。

natural: chase the deer on the central plain

meaning.en: To contend for supremacy: warlords vying for power over the realm; sometimes used of fierce competition in general.
meaning.zh: 群雄争夺天下，也比喻激烈的竞争。

examples.zh: 群雄逐鹿中原，天下大乱。
examples.en: The warlords vied for supremacy, and the realm fell into chaos.

examples.zh: 几家车企在电动车市场逐鹿中原。
examples.en: Several carmakers are fighting for dominance in the electric car market.

story.en: Kuai Tong told Han Xin that when the Qin lost its deer (the throne), all under heaven chased it.
story.zh: 蒯通说：“秦失其鹿，天下共逐之。”

usage.en: Heroic and literary; used for power contests and, figuratively, for business and sport. The deer is a symbol of sovereignty.
usage.zh: 书面语，多指争夺天下，也比喻商战、赛场竞争；“鹿”喻政权。

natural: befriend the far, attack the near

meaning.en: To ally with distant states while attacking neighbouring ones; a stratagem for expansion.
meaning.zh: 联合远方的国家，进攻邻近的国家，是一种外交和军事策略。

equivalents: befriend distant states and strike nearby ones

examples.zh: 秦国采取远交近攻的策略，逐步统一六国。
examples.en: Qin adopted the strategy of befriending the far and attacking the near, gradually uniting the six states.

examples.zh: 在商业竞争中，他也用起了远交近攻的办法。
examples.en: In business he too used the tactic of allying with distant rivals against the nearest.

story.en: Fan Ju advised the King of Qin to befriend distant states and attack the near ones, gaining territory he could actually hold.
story.zh: 范雎对秦昭王说：“王不如远交而近攻，得寸，则王之寸也；得尺，亦王之尺也。”

usage.en: Neutral; a stratagem described in history and in business or diplomacy.
usage.zh: 中性，用于历史、外交和商战策略。
